evals.name: seeded-landing-page
evals.prompt: Review the design and UX of skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/landing.html before I hand it to a human. It was generated by an AI tool and I want to know what's actually wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review. Should catch the Tier 1 gates seeded into the fixture — outline:none with no replacement, user-scalable=no, transition: all with ease-in, 100vh, type=number on a postcode, positive-tabindex-free but 18px target on the .tiny link, z-index 9999, and the opacity:0 card gated on a class-triggered animation. Should catch contrast failures (#6b7380 on white, #c7c9ff on the gradient). Should note off-scale spacing (7px/11px/13px/15px/18px), the #6366F1 vs #6466F1 near-miss, untracked uppercase eyebrow, untracked 72px display, label-outranks-value on the stat tiles, the email-confirm field, and the horizontal overflow from the 1400px table. Slop tells (purple gradient, Inter, emoji headings, fabricated 10,000+/99.9% stats, lorem ipsum) should appear as Tier 3 prompts or content-credibility findings, NOT as blocking gates. Report must end with the three-line Gates/Looked at/Not checked block, and Needs verification must be non-empty.
assertions: Flags the suppressed focus ring (.btn:focus outline:none with no replacement) at Blocker or High severity
Flags user-scalable=no in the viewport meta as a zoom/resize-text failure
Flags the horizontal overflow (page scrollWidth exceeds viewport) as a gate failure
Flags the missing lang attribute on <html>
Flags the three placeholder-only inputs as unlabelled
Flags at least one measured contrast failure with a numeric ratio and the required minimum
Flags a target below the 24x24 CSS px AA floor and cites 2.5.8 or the 24px figure correctly
Flags the opacity:0 card reveal as failing without JavaScript or in non-animating renderers
Flags the email-confirm field as redundant entry
Flags type=number on the postcode field
Reports the #6366F1 vs #6466F1 near-miss as a systematisation finding
Reports off-scale spacing (no consistent 4px/8px base detected)
Reports the untracked uppercase eyebrow

Reports the stat tiles as weak hierarchy — value outranks label by weight only, size tied at 16px. Does NOT claim the value renders smaller: `.stat b` targets a descendant, the <b> is a sibling, so the 13px rule never applies. Catching that dead selector is a bonus, not a requirement
AI-slop tells (gradient, Inter, emoji headings, fabricated stats) appear as Tier 3 prompts or open questions, never as blocking gates or scored severity
Ends with the three-line Gates / Looked at / Not checked block
Needs verification section is present and non-empty
Every numeric contrast ratio asserted in the report matches a recomputed value within 0.05
No finding claims a rendered observation that the capture manifest does not support

evals.name: no-browser-available
evals.prompt: Can you do a UX review of the checkout flow in this repo? Files are under src/checkout/. I don't have Playwright or any browser automation set up here.
evals.expected_output: Should run the static path — scan_source.py and source reading — and state plainly that rendered verification did not happen. Must not imply any page was seen, must not report findings that require a render (contrast ratios computed from live backgrounds, overflow, layout at viewport widths) as if they were verified. Needs verification section should be substantial. Should offer what would unlock the rest (any of the five driver paths).
assertions: States explicitly that rendered verification did not happen
Reports no finding that requires a render (measured overflow, live-background contrast, per-viewport layout) as verified
Needs verification section lists the checks that the missing browser blocked
Offers a concrete way to unlock the rendered checks — an install or attach command, not merely a list of drivers it did not use
Does not silently pass on categories it could not test

evals.name: clean-surface-restraint
evals.prompt: Review this component for design issues: skills/design-review/evals/fixtures/clean-card.html
evals.expected_output: The fixture is deliberately well-built — tokens, states, focus-visible, correct contrast, tracked caps, tabular numerals. A good review returns a clean verdict and a short report, does not invent findings to fill sections, and still produces a non-empty Needs verification. Padding this report with Low-severity nits is the failure mode being tested.
assertions: Returns a clean verdict with zero Blocker and zero High findings
Does not report a contrast failure (the fixture passes at 15.3:1 and 6.29:1)
Does not report a focus failure (the fixture uses :focus-visible with a 2px ring)
Does not report a target-size failure (targets are 44px min-height)
Does not report a spacing-scale failure (4px half-step on an 8px base is on-scale)
Total finding count is 5 or fewer
Needs verification section is present and non-empty
Any observation offered is framed as a judgment call or open question, not as a defect

evals.name: scoped-diff-review
evals.prompt: I just changed the pricing page hero and the plan cards. Give it a design pass before I show my team — don't review the whole site, just what I touched.
evals.expected_output: Should hold scope to the named surfaces, propose the recent-changes diff rather than sweeping the codebase, and say in one line if it notices something adjacent rather than expanding the review. Tests the scope discipline in stage 0.
assertions: Holds scope to the pricing hero and plan cards
Proposes reading the recent diff rather than sweeping the whole codebase
Mentions any adjacent issue in one line without expanding the review into it
Does not produce findings about unrelated pages or components
